deferred_source_units.reason: The generic heading names the sons of Korah and understanding, but does not identify an occasion or a particular external text beyond common title elements.
Remembering God from Jordan, Hermoniim and a small mountain does not identify the speaker or an exile route. The separately read David crossing of Jordan remains an unresolved historical proposal.
The heading gives a familiar designation for the sons of Korah and understanding, without a sufficiently particular external relationship or identified occasion.
The saving from afflicters and shaming of haters is a general retrospective claim with no named rescue or distinctive external correspondence established.

The source says that in God we will be praised, then promises thanksgiving to His name. No specific comparison was established that preserves that passive statement rather than rewriting it as boasting in God.
The abusive speaker and pursuing enemy remain unnamed; their hostile voice alone does not establish a particular event or literary relationship beyond general reproach.

The heart did not withdraw, but God turned the paths away from His way. This unusual assignment of the action is preserved; no target is retained by normalizing it into human apostasy or an unchanged faithful path.

The tongue compared with a swift scribe's reed and the speaker's good word and works for the king have no sufficiently particular external comparison established beyond speaking or writing in general.
The command to gird a sword at the thigh addresses an unnamed royal warrior. Generic equipment or a battle account would not establish a specific relationship or identify this king.
Sharpened arrows in the heart of the king's enemies and peoples falling do not name a battle, enemies or a corresponding historical action; no link is retained merely for arrows or victory.

The fragrant garments and ivory palaces are not identified with the Mosaic holy oil. The separately read recipe shares myrrh but has other ingredients, including iris, and does not establish the same substance or rite.
The king's desire for the daughter's beauty and his designation as her lord do not identify the royal pair. No historical bride or separate Gospel scene is assigned on that basis.
The king's daughter, inward glory and gold-fringed embroidery do not establish identity with priestly garments, a named royal woman or a particular sanctuary object.
The virgin companions brought behind the daughter to the king remain unnamed; a general royal gathering of women does not establish the same procession or participants.
Sons replacing fathers and appointment as rulers throughout the earth are not tied to a named dynasty or genealogy in the actual verse; no such identity is supplied.
The heading concerning hidden things does not itself define those things or identify a musical form, occasion or specific external passage.
The heading names the sons of Korah without further occasion or distinctive interpretive information; a repeated group name alone is not retained.

The repeated commands to make music to God and the King are general praise. The more particular instruction about understanding belongs to the following source unit and is not imported here for another credit.

The rulers gathered with Abraham's God and the earth's mighty ones belonging to God do not state that these rulers are Abraham's descendants or identify a historical assembly; no fulfillment or dynasty is forced.
The gathered kings and their arrival are unnamed and their purpose is unstated. The read comparison with Psalm 2's explicitly hostile rulers remains unresolved rather than identifying the assemblies.
The kings' seeing, astonishment, disturbance and shaking do not identify what they saw or a particular historical defeat; general fear alone is insufficient for a retained connection.
Receiving mercy in the sanctuary is not tied to a particular dedication or narrated act. No specific external relationship was established beyond sanctuary and mercy themes.
The instruction to encircle Zion and recount in her towers is preserved without assigning it to a dated wall procession or a named reconstruction event.
The generic heading for the sons of Korah identifies no particular occasion or external literary relationship beyond the repeated title.
The general invitation for nations and the world's inhabitants to hear is not sufficient by itself to identify a particular external summons or occasion.
The speaker's mouth of wisdom and heart's understanding announce instruction generally; no more particular external relation is established for this unit.
The source says the lawlessness of my heel will surround the speaker. Its difficult expression is not rewritten as enemies at his heels or another familiar reading to obtain a match.

This unit completes the preceding statement with the price of redemption of his soul. It was fully read with verses 8–10, but its necessary grammatical continuation is not awarded a second independent comparison credit.

The sequence ceased forever, will live to the end, will not see corruption and sees wise people dying has difficult relations in this actual text. No target is retained by reversing a negative or substituting a conventional reading about inability to live forever.

The way as a stumbling block and the subsequent delight with their mouth remain difficult as a connected statement; no external target is retained by resolving its pronouns or sequence without evidence.
The prohibition of fear when a person grows rich and his house's glory increases has no sufficiently particular external comparison established beyond general warnings about wealth.

The blessing of the soul during life and the thanks offered to you when you do good have uncertain referential relations. The unit is not turned into a specific rich person's self-address or a narrated feast.
God's manifestation from Zion's beautiful splendor is not assigned to an identified theophany or event; the place and manifestation alone do not establish a specific external connection.

God expressly says He will not rebuke for the sacrifices and that burnt offerings are continually before Him. That statement is not flattened into rejection of all sacrifice to obtain a familiar comparison.

The refusal to receive calves from the house or goats from the flocks belongs to the ensuing ownership and provision argument. No separate external ritual event or more particular parallel was established for this unit alone.

God's ownership of forest animals, mountain beasts and cattle is preserved as this enumeration. No exact external enumeration was established, and the absent familiar thousand-hills wording is not supplied.
The generic David heading alone does not specify the Nathan and Bathsheba episode, which is explicitly given and separately compared in the following unit.
The speaker knows his lawlessness and has his sin continually before him. No more specific external relation was established beyond general acknowledgment or confession of sin.
